diagnosis.classification: fixture/emulator renderer nondeterminism; pinned reference stable
diagnosis.basis: Exactly one eligible framebuffer hash changed only in B2. A1, B1, and A2 produced fdcd25a37910bb25, which also equals the pinned reference and appears in retained Deck and Windows results across OpenGL and Vulkan; ffce5ac91d0966b5 appears only in B2. That evidence makes reference nondeterminism unlikely and points to a transient fixture/emulator renderer or scheduling-sensitive race. A firmware-sensitive scheduling trigger cannot be excluded, but B1 on the same Complex BIOS agrees exactly with both candidate runs, so this does not prove a SpiritBoot regression.

limitations: Pinned Windows/backend framebuffer hashes are retained as informational and are not a Deck correctness oracle. Same-host eligible framebuffer and functional hashes are required to agree exactly across repeats and firmware arms.
Two runs per arm expose gross regressions but do not establish a confidence interval. OS page cache and driver-memory cache are uncontrolled; each run uses a fresh private Mesa disk cache.
